features: THE ORDER THAT ONLY HELD FOR TEN — Two migrations: the database is touched. One creates the table that keeps how many rows each person wants to see on each list; the other adds the matching general setting. Both are additions: no existing table is altered, no data is rewritten, no amount changes. With fifty units shown ten at a time, clicking «Amount ↓» showed the highest of the first ten presented as the highest in the list.

REPORTED ON THE FORUM, BY SOMEONE WHO HAD WORKED IT OUT. «If I have 50 records but the view is filtered to 10 at a time, the sorting only applies to those 10.» Checking confirmed the scale: twenty-six tables with server-side pagination, zero that sent the sorting to the server. Every one of them sorted the rows it already held. It is a defect that raises no error and leaves no trace: the screen is consistent with itself and answers falsely.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE SAME DEFECT. A second administrator had reported something that did not look related: «in the buildings list I search having set 40 items per page, and only 10 come out». The table built each request on its own, remembering only what it needed: searching lost the rows per page and the sorting, changing page lost the filters. Now filter, page, rows and sorting always travel together.

TABLES NOW REMEMBER WHO USES THEM. The rows chosen on a list are there again on return, per person and per list: someone who sets 50 on invoices and 10 on documents finds 50 on invoices and 10 on documents, and the choice does not land on anyone else. General settings now carry «Rows per page in lists», the starting value for those who have not chosen yet. It stops at 50 rather than 100, because the resident portal has no row selector and so high a global value would hand residents a hundred cards with no way to reduce them.

SORTING IS NOT REMEMBERED, AND THAT IS A DECISION. The third click on a header is the one that returns a list to its natural order, and it reaches the server as a request that says nothing about sorting — indistinguishable from «I did not mention it». With a stored sort that click would stop working on every table, without any error: remembering it would cost the ability to remove it. Filters are not remembered either, for a simpler reason: a remembered filter makes rows disappear without anyone having asked.

COLUMNS THAT ARE NOT FIELDS NO LONGER SORT. «Location» assembles block, stairwell and floor; «Parties» holds a list of people. Sorting on a cell that holds a list would mean sorting by how many people are in it, which is not what the person clicking is asking for. Those headers are no longer clickable, and the server does not accept those keys either. Every sort now carries the primary key as its second criterion: without it the database guarantees nothing between tied rows, and the same row could appear on two pages while another appears on none.

THE ROW COUNT HAD SIX DIFFERENT RULES AND NO CEILING. The same parameter was validated six ways: with no limit in fifteen requests, with different ceilings in nine more, and in the F24 forms it was not validated at all. A ?per_page=1000000 went through and landed straight in a LIMIT: no malice required, just a finger on a zero. There is now a single list of accepted values, and it is the same list the selector shows. A value outside it is ignored rather than rejected, because rejecting it would turn a legitimate bookmark into an error that sends the user back with no explanation.

THE SELECTOR DID NOT CONTAIN ITS OWN VALUE. It offered 15, 20, 30, 40 and 50 while the default was 10: anyone who moved to 50 could no longer find the option to go back, because it had never been in the menu. The list is now the one the server accepts, and the value in use always appears in it. The general ledger keeps its own starting value of twenty rows: entries are dense and a working day easily produces more than ten.

WHAT THE REVIEW FOUND BEFORE RELEASE. Eight defects, all fixed, and five were the original reported defect in forms nobody would have looked for. Six lists — announcements, reports and documents, in both the administrator and portal versions — sorted by date whatever column was asked for, because the shared service applied its own ORDER BY before the chosen one: the trait now clears whatever ordering it finds, because asking to sort means «you decide the order». The calendar could not sort at all — recurrences are generated in PHP and there is no ORDER BY to lean on — and four headers were clickable to no effect: they no longer are. The F24 forms declared four sortable columns and did not sort. Instalment plans and charts of accounts did not paginate at all, because of a route that does not exist: a defect older than this version, surfacing now because it is the first time anyone checked that those tables paginate. The users list would have errored when sorting by contact record, the day a user had two. And the memory filled itself: even a plain «page 2» was taken for a choice, and from then on the general setting would have moved nothing.

UPDATES ON YOUR OWN SERVER. Two forum reports in the same week — an Ubuntu machine with NGINX, an LXC container with Debian — brought out the same thing: the whole install and update procedure had been designed around shared hosting, where the server's public folder and the project root are the same place thanks to the rules the installer itself writes. On a properly configured server, with the web root pointing at public/, the update file was simply unreachable from the browser: updating meant moving the server root back and forth every time, and for those minutes the entire project folder — configuration file included — was served to the web. The setup file now recognises where it is and works correctly whether it is uploaded into the project root or inside public/. In the one genuinely ambiguous case — a fresh installation inside an empty folder named public — it asks which of the two folders to use, showing both paths in full, instead of guessing; and it refuses to run if it would take the place of Laravel's main file, which would leave the site unreachable. This applies to first-time installation too, not only to updates: it was the same obstacle.

THE «UPDATE NOW» BUTTON ON SERVERS SERVING public/. It had the same limitation and has been fixed: the update engine is now placed inside the public folder and receives the project path from Laravel instead of deducing it from its own location. Mind when the fix actually takes effect, because it is not what it looks like: during an update the code that runs is always the one of the version you are leaving, not the one you are taking. Anyone arriving at 1.10 from a 1.9.x will therefore still use the old mechanism, and on that kind of server will have to update using the setup file; from 1.10 onwards the button works everywhere. Two smaller defects of the same mechanism were fixed alongside: the updates page no longer stays stuck on «update in progress» when a launch does not go through — the exchange file has a declared expiry and it is now honoured — and leftover copies of the update engine are finally recognised and removed, because the cleanup was looking for a signature that file never contained.

THE PREVIOUS VERSION'S ASSETS NO LONGER PILE UP. Compiled interface files carry a fingerprint of their content in the name, so the old ones were never overwritten by the new ones and nobody removed them: one real update between two betas left three hundred and seventy-five behind, and it happened at every update. They are now removed, but only after the system integrity check: never before, because an update interrupted halfway would leave the site with no interface files at all — a blank page instead of an old but working version.

WHAT THIS VERSION DOES NOT DO. The resident portal has no tables: announcements, events, reports and documents are shown as cards, with no sortable headers and no row selector. The defect did not exist there and there was nothing to fix. Clamping the page to the last available one stays out: a ?page=7 bookmark on a list that has three still gives an empty table. It is a real defect but an earlier one, not made worse by this version.
